gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Toybox, its pick for younger children, can only join a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network (Toybox: "The printer can't connect to a 5G network") and is set up by linking it to an online Toybox account, with a code the printer shows only once it is connected to the internet.
standout_why: I compared against printingxyz.com, which discusses Toybox burn risk and the app but says nothing about Wi-Fi band, internet or accounts, and itechguides.com, which lists only 'Wi-Fi' as a Toybox spec and gives a band and offline mode only for the Tina2C. I could not read the cited Tom's Hardware guide (https://www.tomshardware.com/3d-printing/best-3d-printers-for-kids-and-teens): WebFetch returned only its 30,155-character navigation menu, so I can't rule out that it covers this. I did not open the other nine results.
decides: This confirms the Toybox for ages 5–8, but only for homes with a working 2.4 GHz band and internet access. On a 5 GHz-only network, or a dual-band mesh where Toybox says the 5G network 'will prevent connection', setup can fail. In that case the Bambu A1 mini or the Adventurer 5M Pro is the safer pick. Flashforge added a LAN mode to the 5M series in firmware, so that printer does not depend on a cloud account.
